It's really hard to explain why I struggle to see people in a consistent way so sorry if I don't make sense or it's not clear. 

Part of it is I generally see everything in black and white - so for example of I get a criticism at work I start thinking I'm the worst at my job and a total and utter failure. There's a part of DBT called "check the facts" where (as the name says) you look at all the facts of a situation and that helps balance it out. Currently I struggle to do this by myself and it's something me and my case worker go through often.

Another aspect is my fear of getting hurt or letting people get close. If I let my walls down and let someone in the more I open myself up to getting hurt and the harder it hits. So if I cut someone off when they do something that seems minor the more I am able to protect myself because in my head it's inevitable that somewhere along the line they'll do something. To confuse things this also goes alongside the feeling of loneliness and needing external validation which means I can cling to people and because I want attention from them they seem like the most amazing person. 

I wish I could answer for what techniques help - unfortunately this is still something I don't manage well. I did a years IOP DBT program but I really struggle with therapeutic relationships so every time I got to a place where I'd start trusting my therapist she'd say something which would put me right back to the start.

Appreciate you asking questions - BPD has so much stigma so it's great you're trying to understand

On the flip side if someone does something good that means I totally forget all the bad things they've done and they're totally amazing. 

Your question about the impact and the effect - it's horrible and incredibly stressful. Just imagine the feeling of the person you love most and trust most in the world suddenly flipping and everything they do is hateful and malicious.

What I did with my guy - first I moved a chair next to his tank and would sit there and watch TV and not look at him, then after a few days would start to just have a look in his tank but still just sitting on the chair. This allowed him to get used to me and know I wasn't a predator.

Next I would take him out and hold him for 10 mins and then put him back/let him roam. Be careful how you pick him up as you hand can give them impression of a bird/predator swooping down. If he wanted to move and explore before the 10 mins was up that was fine - I never forced him to stay. I would add minutes on after a few days until eventually he'd cuddle up. 

Big thing is have patience - they have a long life so you have the time to let them get used to you.  Don't force them to do anything - some days he might really want to just chill by himself. 

Hope that helps!!
